name: Watermelon
lede: Watermelon is the red-pink of the fruit's flesh, a food color name recorded in a 1930 color dictionary and again in the 2010 xkcd survey.

sections.title: A fruit name
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's dictionary of 1930 records the name, with a first appearance dated 1926 and a plate position of 1 K 9 [1]. The xkcd survey of 2010 lists it again [1]. The flesh gets its red mostly from lycopene, the same pigment that colors tomatoes, and which Paterson says also colors apricots, pink grapefruit and guavas [2]. Nearest named colors are [[lightish-red]], [[grapefruit]] and [[fiery-rose]] [3].

sections.title: A dye-vat simile
sections.body: Finlay describes a madder lake being made by George Field's method: crushed roots are washed, the dye is mixed with alum and water, and the froth-topped slurry looks like watermelon juice [4]. The comparison is the writer's, not a trade name, but it shows how a natural red-pink reads to the eye. See [[flower:madder|madder]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only 2 paintings in our archive of 23,781 hold this color, as photographed, which makes it rarer than 79% of named colors [5]. The word itself peaks in printed English in the 2010s, and rose fastest in the 1880s [6]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, not pigment tests.
